<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Add another check to abort if migration has already happened. Was able to reproduce the bug that was reported by:
* Run 2023.9.0
* Add devices
* Upgrade to 2023.9.2
* Restart twice (not sure why you sometimes has to restart twice, sometimes not)
* Some entities are already migrated, but the migration was not aborted

Adding a "late exit" to abort in those cases. And not sure why it's not always happening.

I'm experiencing the same behavior. The old entities (pre 2023.9) were back immediately after upgrading to 2023.9.2. However, after rebooting they're all (old and new) unavailable.

For me the new ones work.

Seems to have changed from "sensor.airthings_wave_124763_temperature" to "sensor.airthings_wave_temperature".
Previously I recall it was the other way around. Seems like I have to re-add them to my dashboard every major release with a different name :D
I ended up downgrading to 2023.9.1 to get airthings working again.

Can confirm same issue on 2023.9.2..

Edit: Seems like owner mentioned it will be fixed in 2023.9.3 :)

review_comments: Side note: I don't think we should use MockEntity for those constants, `VOC_V1` etc, as they are not used as entities. Just use a dataclass or a dict or similar to capture those values.
